I have farmed in Quzhou County for 40 years, so I would keep to the pattern I know works here: wheat followed by maize on most of my land, and cotton on the rest. Because some people in my family work off-farm, I would not choose a plan that is too complicated or too labor-intensive. I have well irrigation, so I would use that to protect wheat at key stages and to help maize establish in summer if rain is uneven. I would use improved or hybrid seed where it gives me stable yield, and I would keep fertilizer moderate and practical instead of pushing too hard. For wheat, I would focus on steady population, enough base fertilizer, and a few irrigations around the important growth stages. For maize, I would use hybrid seed, simpler field management, and fewer irrigations because summer rain can help. For cotton, I would keep a smaller area because it takes more management, but I would still plant it because I know how to manage it and it spreads my risk. I would use rotary tillage because it fits my machinery conditions and saves time, and I would aim for stable yields rather than chasing the maximum.
